entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bérenger Frédol the Elder (d. 1323), a distinguished French canon lawyer and Cardinal-Bishop of Frascati, played a pivotal role in shaping papal jurisprudence during the tumultuous Avignon Papacy. Born in the late 13th century in the diocese of Béziers, he rose through ecclesiastical ranks, becoming a key intellectual and administrative force within the Curia. His career spanned the reigns of several popes, most notably Clement V and John XXII, for whom he served as a trusted advisor and legal expert, contributing significantly to the consolidation of papal authority and the codification of canon law.

Frédol's most enduring contribution was his involvement in the compilation and revision of the *Clementines*, a collection of papal decrees issued by Clement V and later promulgated by John XXII in 1317. This collection, which included decrees from the Council of Vienne (1311–1312) and other papal constitutions, aimed to clarify and update the existing body of canon law. As a skilled jurist, Frédol's expertise was crucial in organizing these complex legal texts, ensuring their coherence and enforceability across the Catholic world. His work on the *Clementines* solidified his reputation as one of the preeminent legal minds of his era, directly influencing the administration of justice within the Church.

The *Clementines*, largely shaped by Frédol's legal acumen, became an integral part of the *Corpus Juris Canonici*, the foundational legal text of the Catholic Church, remaining in force for centuries. His efforts helped to standardize ecclesiastical legal practice and reinforced the Pope's legislative supremacy at a time when papal authority faced challenges from secular rulers and internal dissent. Frédol's legacy thus extends beyond his lifetime, as his contributions to canon law continued to inform legal scholarship and ecclesiastical governance, influencing generations of jurists and shaping the institutional structure of the Church.

entities.summary:
Berengar Fredol or Bérenger Frédol was a French canon lawyer and Cardinal-Bishop of Frascati.
He played a significant role in shaping the Catholic Church's legal and administrative structures during the late Middle Ages.
Born in 1250 in France, Fredol rose to prominence through his education at the University of Paris and his appointment as a canon at the Notre-Dame Cathedral.

As a key figure in the Curia Romana, Fredol contributed to the development of the Canon Law, a collection of ecclesiastical laws that governed the Church's internal affairs.
He also participated in several synods and councils, including the Council of Vienne, where he played a crucial role in resolving theological disputes.

Fredol's legacy extends beyond his contributions to the Canon Law, as he also helped establish the office of the Cardinal-Bishop of Frascati, a position that would become increasingly powerful during the Renaissance.
This institution became a hub for papal politics and a center of influence for the Catholic Church in Italy.

The legacy of Berengar Fredol can be seen in the continued relevance of the Canon Law, which remains an important part of Catholic canon.
The modern Catholic Church still uses many of the principles established by Fredol during his time as Cardinal-Bishop of Frascati.
